About Council and standing committee meetings

Council holds different types of meetings, including ordinary, special and budget Council meetings, and regular standing committee meetings.

These meetings are where all Councillors meet in the Council Chamber to debate issues and make formal decisions for the city.

Council considers matters such as budgets, policies, local laws, planning initiatives and recommendations from standing committees.

Members of the public are welcome to attend any Council meeting. In some circumstances, parts of a meeting may be closed when confidential matters are being discussed. 

Ordinary Council and standing committee meetings are held weekly on Tuesdays, except during recess periods. 

All meetings are held at Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane.

Council's standing committees

Council has 9 standing committees made up of elected representatives. Committees advise on a range of areas, including infrastructure, public transport and the environment.

The Establishment and Coordination Committee, also known as Civic Cabinet, has been delegated significant responsibility by full Council. Civic Cabinet meets weekly to discuss policies and strategies in areas such as:

  • major projects
  • finance
  • urban planning
  • transport
  • environment
  • community services
  • city businesses
  • Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

It is in this way that Civic Cabinet sets the strategic direction for Brisbane as a city and for Brisbane City Council as an organisation. The members of Civic Cabinet review and make recommendations to full Council on major plans such as Council's vision, City Plan, corporate documents and city finances.

Committee responsibilities

The responsibilities of the City Planning, Suburban Renewal and Economic Development Committee will be to:

  • plan for the sustainable development of Brisbane to ensure economic prosperity and maintain quality of life
  • plan for a growing city by ensuring that Brisbane City Plan 2014 remains current, efficient and effective
  • collaborate with Queensland Government authorities and other local governments in regional planning and to implement the Queensland Government’s ShapingSEQ South East Queensland Regional Plan 2023 as it pertains to the Brisbane Local Government Area
  • plan sustainable neighbourhoods where Brisbane residents want to live and work
  • deliver on the outcomes of Brisbane’s Future Blueprint, Brisbane: Our Productive City, Brisbane’s Sustainable Growth Strategy and Brisbane’s Housing Supply Action Plan
  • ensure Brisbane retains the unique character of its architecture and natural attributes
  • promote a range of housing choices to cater for Brisbane’s diverse population
  • partner with the property and construction industry to ensure the sustainable development of Brisbane
  • deliver improvement projects in suburban precincts
  • undertake integrated medium and long-term planning for Council across land use, open space, public and active transport, economic development and community facilities through the local government infrastructure plan and long term infrastructure plan process
  • work with local communities, industry and other levels of government to facilitate suburban renewal projects in Brisbane’s suburbs
  • facilitate high-quality, sustainable urban design and private and public art to foster inclusive, vibrant and liveable communities
  • oversee and manage integrated, efficient and effective permitting and streamlined development assessment process
  • decide delegated applications during recess
  • recommend major project applications to Council for consideration
  • enhance Brisbane’s economic position
  • ensure that small business is supported with Council programs and events
  • promote and integrate Brisbane’s marketing and business attraction opportunities
  • promote investment in Brisbane
  • manage Brisbane’s Economic Development Plan and implement its recommendations
  • deliver local Business Partnership Initiatives and other measures which support Brisbane business at any level of growth
  • ensure the successful operation of Brisbane Economic Development Agency
  • encourage new opportunities in the tourism sector
  • work with the small business community to ensure Council is responsive to the needs of the sector and supportive of the creation of local jobs
  • work with the business community to enhance the nighttime economy, including in key precincts of Brisbane, such as Fortitude Valley and the Central Business District
  • develop strong relationships with the multicultural communities of Brisbane and maintain strong relationships with Council’s Sister Cities
  • advance Brisbane’s global positioning and international relationships with key regions to facilitate business and trade connections
  • deliver on Council’s Olympic Host Contract commitments and obligations relating to the portfolio.

Committee responsibilities

The responsibilities of the Community and the Arts Committee will be to:

  • develop vibrant and caring local Brisbane communities
  • provide and promote opportunities for Brisbane residents to have an active and healthy lifestyle
  • provide pools, community halls and meeting spaces for Brisbane residents
  • support exciting, vibrant cultural and artistic activities for Brisbane residents including oversight of Brisbane Powerhouse and Museum of Brisbane
  • partner with community and business organisations to sponsor and deliver community services
  • provide high-quality community venues and recreation facilities
  • manage Council’s relationships with community groups that operate from Council-owned facilities and provide support to improve and maintain facilities
  • work with sporting organisations to support community-based sport and recreation activities
  • deliver on the outcomes in Brisbane’s Sustainable Growth Strategy as it relates to homelessness and community housing providers
  • deliver strategies and programs that acknowledge and value the unique contributions that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples make to Brisbane, including overseeing the implementation of Brisbane City Council’s Innovate Reconciliation Action Plan
  • deliver on Council’s Olympic Host Contract commitments and obligations relating to the portfolio
  • oversee, in partnership with the Queensland Government, the Major Brisbane Festivals entity, delivering Brisbane Festival.

  • deliver on the goals in Council’s Brisbane: Clean, Green, Sustainable including natural habitat cover
  • partner with the community and businesses and support volunteer organisations in their contribution to the protection and enhancement of Brisbane’s environment
  • oversee and manage waste management and resource recovery for Brisbane residents
  • ensure citywide litter prevention
  • implement the Brisbane Off-Road Cycling Strategy
  • maintain and enhance Brisbane's drainage network
  • prepare Council and the community to minimise the impact of severe weather and natural disasters
  • ensure coordination with the State Emergency Services during localised incident and disaster response activities
  • ensure the successful operation of Brisbane Sustainability Agency and City Parklands Services
  • deliver on Council’s Olympic Host Contract commitments and obligations relating to the portfolio.

  • ensure the management of the capital works program for the optimum performance of Council’s road network

Get involved

You can attend Council meetings as an observer or alternatively watch the livestream and recordings. You can also read previous meeting minutes.

Ways to communicate local issues with Council

  • Contact your local Councillor via phone, email or letter
  • Contact the relevant Standing Committee Civic Cabinet Chair via phone, email or letter
  • Contact the CEO or Lord Mayor via email or letter
  • Lodge a public petition to have your views formally presented and investigated by Council
  • Provide a submission during community consultation periods on local matters.

To discuss any other issues affecting your community, see our community engagement opportunities. 

Council Ordinary Meetings are held in the Council Chamber at Brisbane City Hall. Meeting agendas are published before each meeting.

Limited seating is available in the Public Gallery. The Public Gallery is located in an elevated area overlooking the Council Chamber and is accessed by stairs. City Hall staff will direct visitors to the designated viewing area.

Visitors who are unable to access the Public Gallery can be accommodated in an accessible viewing area within the Council Chamber.

For more information, phone Council on 07 3403 8888 or learn about accessibility at City Hall.

You can also take a virtual tour of the Council Chamber.

Rules of attendance

All attendees need to follow behavioural guidelines so Council meetings can run smoothly and cover all items on the agenda.

Council meetings

If you attend a Council meeting, you’re bound by Meetings Local Law 2001 and the Conditions of Entry to:

  • remain silent
  • not interrupt the conduct of business
  • not record or photograph from the Public Gallery without approval from the Chair of Council.
Standing Committee meetings

If you attend a Standing Committee meeting, you must not:

  • interrupt the meeting
  • speak at any time
  • enter or leave the room after the meeting has started
  • argue with the Civic Cabinet Chair if they ask you to leave.

You can apply to speak at Council meetings. Requests to address Council are at the discretion of the Chair of Council.

Before you apply

Council receives a high number of applications to address Council and not all applications or preferred dates can be accommodated. The Chair of Council may determine that your matter is better addressed through a more suitable pathway and Council may contact you to discuss.

Who can apply

To be considered, your request should relate to a matter of public interest, fall within Council’s responsibility and be suitable to be raised in a public meeting.

Applications may be declined or redirected where the subject is:

  • an individual or private matter
  • an operational service request
  • a matter already considered or under investigation by Council
  • a regulatory or statutory matter better handled through the relevant process
  • containing defamatory, offensive or irrelevant material.

How to apply

1. Download the application to address Council.

What happens next

If the Chair of Council approves your application, we will contact you as soon as possible with an available speaking date and the protocols you’ll need to follow.

If you’re approved

  • You'll have a maximum of 5 minutes to speak.
  • No one in the meeting can interrupt you.
  • Council can’t debate any issue you raise.
  • The Lord Mayor or the Civic Cabinet Chair of the relevant Standing Committee may respond on Council's behalf, and you must not interrupt or debate any of the issues.

Following your address, you are welcome to watch the remainder of the Council meeting from the Public Gallery.

Privacy and public recording

Council meetings are livestreamed, recorded and transcribed for inclusion in Council’s minutes. The minutes and recording are published on Council’s website. By applying to speak, you acknowledge that your name and the content of your address will be published as part of the public record.

Things to remember:

  • ‘Streaming paused for Meeting adjournment’ means the meeting will begin again shortly
  • recordings are uploaded to Council’s YouTube channel after each livestream.

    Council meeting minutes are a written record of everything that is said in the Council Chamber during an ordinary meeting. This includes:

    • speeches by public speakers 
    • question time
    • standing committee presentations
    • resolutions adopted by Council
    • new questions raised that require further investigation (known as questions on notice)
